tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final answer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After solving the puzzle, present the complete sequence of moves as a single list in the exact required format.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you have generated the full move sequence for the Tower of Hanoi problem and are ready to output the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Providing extra explanatory text after the move list or omitting moves, causing the parser to read an empty or incorrect list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Free blocked larger disks by moving top smaller disks first
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If a larger disk you need to move is not the topmost disk on its peg, first relocate any smaller disks that are on top of it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a disk that is blocked by smaller disks on its source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 4 while disk 2 sits on top of it, resulting in an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate source peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Check that the disk you intend to move is the topmost disk on its source peg; moving any other disk violates the rules.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before committing to each move in the sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 5 while disk 1 is on top of it, causing an illegal source selection.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate destination peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Ensure that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk; otherwise the move is illegal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before each move, check the top disk of the destination peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing disk 4 onto a peg where disk 2 is on top, which is smaller.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Apply classic Hanoi recursion to generate move sequence
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When you need to transfer a contiguous stack of k disks from one peg to another using the third peg, recursively move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, move the largest disk, then move the k‑1 disks onto the target.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you have to move a stack of disks as a whole, especially when the goal is a single‑peg stack.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move three disks directly without recursively handling the sub‑stack, leading to missing moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear destination peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the destination peg currently holds smaller disks that must end up above the larger disk in the final configuration, move those smaller disks elsewhere before moving the larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before moving a larger disk onto a peg that already contains smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 5 onto a peg where disk 4 is already placed, violating the final ordering.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Goal‑first descending placement
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When the goal is to stack all disks on a single peg, prioritize moving the largest remaining disk to the goal peg first, then handle the next largest, and so on.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: In problems where the final configuration is a single stacked peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Delaying the move of the largest disk while moving smaller ones first, causing extra moves or deadlock.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate final configuration after move generation
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing the move list, simulate the moves from the initial state to verify that the final configuration matches the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After you have generated the complete move list, before outputting it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Submitting a move list that leaves some disks on the wrong peg, resulting in a mismatch with the goal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use the smallest disk as a flexible temporary placeholder
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Treat the smallest disk (disk 1) as a universal temporary buffer; it can be placed on any larger disk and moved freely to free up other pegs.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need a temporary spot to hold a disk while moving larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Failing to use disk 1 as a buffer, leading to a situation where no legal move is available.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may stop generating output prematurely or think no moves are needed.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always generate at least one move if the initial state differs from the goal, and verify the move list is non‑empty before finalizing.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Truncated move list (incomplete solution) due to token limit
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model runs out of tokens before finishing the full sequence of moves.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Plan the solution to fit within the token budget, or generate moves incrementally and ensure the final list is complete.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk (source peg top mismatch)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model selects a disk that is blocked by smaller disks on its peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Check that the chosen disk is the topmost on its source peg before moving it.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (illegal placement)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model does not verify the size ordering on the destination peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Ensure the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Extra list after move list causing parser to read wrong answer
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model adds additional brackets or explanatory text after the move list.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Place the move list as the final element of the response and avoid any trailing text.
